result.topic_en: Corollaries on excluding the cases of lower formulas when counting the proper cases (residues x) for which x^n - 1 is divisible by a prime, followed by the statement of a problem to determine the number of proper cases for every exponent n.
result.transcription:
96 RESIDVA EX DIVIS. POTESTATVM
Coroll. 1.
31. Quia caſus $x=1$ formulae $x^n-1$ cum omnibus inferioribus eſt communis, hunc ſemper a caſibus formulae iſti propriis excludi oportet; vnde cum numerus omnium caſuum ſit $n$, numerus caſuum propriorum ſaltem vnitate eſt minor.
Coroll. 2.
32. Si exponens $n$ fuerit numerus primus, formula $x^n-1$ per nullam inferiorem eiusdem formae diuiſibilis eſt praeter $x^1-1$, vnde numerus caſuum propriorum eſt $n-1$.
Coroll. 3.
33. Sin autem exponens $n$ fuerit numerus compoſitus puta $n=\mu\nu$, tum formula $x^n-1$ iisdem caſibus eſt diuiſibilis, quibus formulae $x^\mu-1$ et $x^\nu-1$, quandoquidem ipſa per has diuiſibilis exiſtit; vnde caſus harum formularum a caſibus propriis formulae $x^n-1$ ſunt ſegregandi.
Problema.
34. Pro omnibus exponentibus $n$ numerum caſuum propriorum definire, quibus formula $x^n-1$ per quempiam numerum primum P diuiſibilis reddi poteſt, alios pro $x$ valores non admittendo, niſi qui diuiſore ſint minores.
Solutio.

items.quote: Si exponens $n$ fuerit numerus primus, formula $x^n-1$ per nullam inferiorem eiusdem formae diuiſibilis eſt praeter $x^1-1$, vnde numerus caſuum propriorum eſt $n-1$.
items.english: If the exponent n is a prime number, the formula x^n - 1 is divisible by no lower formula of the same form except x^1 - 1, whence the number of proper cases is n - 1.

items.quote: Pro omnibus exponentibus $n$ numerum caſuum propriorum definire, quibus formula $x^n-1$ per quempiam numerum primum P diuiſibilis reddi poteſt, alios pro $x$ valores non admittendo, niſi qui diuiſore ſint minores.
items.english: For all exponents n, to determine the number of proper cases in which the formula x^n - 1 can be made divisible by some prime number P, admitting no other values for x than those smaller than the divisor.
